blocks.content: The inclination of the Earth's axis at an angle of 23.5 degrees to the perpendicular of its orbital plane is the primary cause of seasonal variations on Earth.

rows: Plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earth's axis is an imaginary line running through its center from the North Pole to the South Pole.
The axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5° from the perpendicular to its orbital plane.
The angle made by Earth's axis with its orbital plane is 66.5°.
Parallelism of the axis means Earth's tilt always points toward Polaris (the North Star) as it orbits the Sun.
The combination of axial tilt and revolution around the Sun causes the changing of seasons.
Exams frequently test the difference between the tilt angle relative to the normal (23.5°) and relative to the orbital plane (66.5°).
Remember that Earth rotates from West to East, making celestial bodies appear to move East to West.
The circle of illumination divides the lit side from the dark side of Earth and does not coincide with the axis of rotation due to the tilt.
